about: Repairs pack-check applies for a cause proven in a real run. A fixed repair names its loader and game versions, a match read from the jars before the game runs (mod-below, mod-range, mods-together, dependency-unmet, dependency-missing), the check that shows the fault in the game, an action (add-jar, remove-mod, replace-mod) whose download is checked against its SHA-512, the evidence, and a test. A rule (loader and minecraft "*") names a kind of fault instead: a file the pack's host no longer serves (unavailable-file), a library no jar provides or one pinned to another version (dependency-missing and dependency-unmet with mod "*"), a server-optional mod that stops the server (start-failure); "when": "start-failed" reads it from a failed start's log. Its action (substitute-file, fetch-dependency, leave-out-of-server) finds the file at run time from a source that publishes a size or hash and checks the jar's own metadata. Every entry's test (jars, and unavailable files or a log where the match reads them) must match before the action and not after it (run by self-test). A finding with no entry here is reported with its evidence and left alone.

fixes.symptom: A world opens the first time and never again: "Failed to load datapacks, can't proceed with server load", caused by "Overworld settings missing".
fixes.cause: Biolith before 1.0.1-beta.1 adds placeholder climate points (3.01, outside the -2..2 the game reads back) for the biomes it places. When another mod saves the overworld's biome list in full (Blueprint's modded biome source does), the next start rejects that entry and the overworld is dropped.
evidence: pack-check on Prehistoric World 2 2.4.0 (Forge 47.4.20), 2026-10-30: Traverse 7.0.12 bundles Biolith 1.0.1-alpha.1; the second start fails; with 1.0.1-beta.1 added the second start opens, every placed block reads back, and a world saved by the broken version opens too
fixes.why: Forge loads the highest version of a library that is both bundled inside another mod and present on its own, so the newer jar in the mods folder replaces the copy bundled inside Traverse.

test.from: Traverse 7.0.12 for Forge bundles Biolith 1.0.1-alpha.1 (Prehistoric World 2 2.4.0)

fixes.symptom: The game does not start: Forge stops with "Mod soulsweapons requires projectile_damage 3.2.2+1.20.1" because the pack has Projectile Damage 3.2.3+1.20.1.
fixes.cause: Marium's Soulslike Weaponry before 1.4 (1.2.x and 1.3.x for Forge 1.20.1) pins projectile_damage to exactly [3.2.2+1.20.1]; Projectile Damage's current Forge release is 3.2.3+1.20.1, so a pack that takes the newest library does not load. Soulslike Weaponry 1.4.4 drops the dependency.
evidence: soulslike-weaponry-1.2.4-1.20.1-forge.jar and 1.3.1 META-INF/mods.toml: projectile_damage versionRange="[3.2.2+1.20.1]"; 1.4.4 has no projectile_damage dependency

pack-check --fix on JoJo's Bizarre Modpack 1.0.0 (Modrinth .mrpack, Forge 47.4.3, 108 files), 2026-11-14: the shipped pack's server stops at start-up and its log names soulsweapons; the repaired pack, run beside it, makes a new world, places 4,515 block items, opens the world again and reads all 4,474 placed blocks back; the fixed .mrpack it writes passes pack-check on its own
fixes.why: Projectile Damage 3.2.2 is the version Soulslike Weaponry was built against and still provides the projectile_damage id other mods read; replacing the library keeps every mod of the pack, where updating Soulslike Weaponry to 1.4 would change its content.

fixes.symptom: A player cannot install the pack as published: a mod file its manifest lists is no longer served by CurseForge.
fixes.cause: CurseForge removes files (an author deletes a version, a project is archived); an export keeps naming the old file id, and CurseForge publishes no hash, so the same bytes cannot be found anywhere else.

action.how: The same CurseForge project's file for the pack's game version and loader, the nearest newer one first: checked against the size CurseForge publishes, its own metadata (a mod for this loader and game version, inside every range the pack's mods require its ids in), and against Modrinth's SHA-1 where Modrinth has it. A project with no such file is left out of the fixed pack with a note; the pack was checked without it.

fixes.why: The project is the same mod; its next file for the same game version and loader is the smallest change a pack author would make, and the repaired pack's server proves it before the user's pack changes.

test.from: All the Mods 9 1.1.1 (CurseForge, Forge 47.4.0): LionfishAPI file 5922047 is gone; CurseForge still serves 2.7 for Forge 1.20.1

fixes.symptom: The game does not start: the loader stops because a mod requires a library no jar in the pack provides.
fixes.cause: The library's file is no longer served by the pack's host, or the pack never listed it.

action.how: The version the dependant's own Modrinth release names (found by the dependant jar's SHA-1), else the oldest Modrinth release for the pack's game version and loader that every dependant accepts; checked against Modrinth's SHA-512 and its own metadata.

fixes.why: The dependant's author names the exact library release it was built against; failing that, the oldest release in range is closest to what the pack was made with.

fixes.symptom: The game does not start: the loader stops because a mod requires a library in a version other than the one the pack has.
fixes.cause: A mod pins a library (often to one exact version) and the pack took the library's newest release.

action.how: The library in a version every dependant in the pack accepts: the one the dependant's own Modrinth release names, else the oldest such Modrinth release for the pack's game version and loader; checked against Modrinth's SHA-512 and its own metadata. It replaces the pack's copy.

fixes.why: Pinning the library keeps every mod of the pack; updating the dependant would change its content.

patterns: Could not execute entrypoint stage '(?:server|main)' due to errors, provided by '([a-z0-9_\-]+)'

fixes.symptom: The server does not start: a mod's own start-up code fails on a dedicated server, though the mod is one a server does not need.
fixes.cause: A mod made for the client (its Modrinth page or the pack says a server may go without it) runs client set-up when a server starts and fails there.

action.how: The server leaves the jar out; players keep it. A fixed .mrpack marks its file env.server "unsupported" (or moves a jar it carries to client-overrides).

fixes.why: The mod's own author says a server does not need it, so leaving it off the server changes nothing a player sees.
